title: Rosalind and the Promise
premise: Sebastian Joubert, a ghostwriter who fled a scandal five years ago and now lives by careful increments, is hired to write the memoirs of vintner Marguerite Ashcombe — only to discover the deed to her beloved orchard lists two estranged names: hers and Rosalind's, the woman Sebastian once loved and abandoned. As harvest approaches and a predatory developer circles the failing vineyard, Sebastian must choose between his contract's confidentiality and the truth that could save both the land and his own capacity for love. In the end, he betrays the memoir deal to expose the developer's fraud, Rosalind chooses him over her inherited duty to sell, and the first harvest comes in under both their names.
about_author: Elodie Oyelaran is a former sommelier who traded tasting notes for love stories set among vines and old family grievances. She writes from a converted barn in the countryside, where she keeps a stubborn orchard of her own.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Five years after a public disgrace ended his writing career and his engagement, he ghostwrites celebrity memoirs under strict anonymity, measuring life in cautious routines. A new commission arrives: the memoirs of celebrated vintner Marguerite Ashcombe. Beat: the cost of safety established.

chapters.title: The Deed That Wouldn't Behave
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At Ashcombe Vineyard, Marguerite's lawyer produces an old orchard deed that stubbornly names two owners: Marguerite and 'R. Okafor.' Sebastian recognizes the initial — Rosalind, the woman he left. He says nothing. Beat: dread disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Version
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Interview sessions begin; Marguerite is brilliant, controlling, and evasive about the orchard and about a woman she calls 'the promise I broke.' Sebastian senses the memoir's real story is being withheld — from him and perhaps from herself. Beat: curiosity sharpening into unease.

chapters.title: Rosalind, Present Tense
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind returns to the valley after years abroad, summoned by the deed dispute and her aunt Marguerite's failing health. She learns a stranger has been installed in the guest cottage as biographer. Beat: homecoming laced with resentment and unfinished grief.

chapters.title: First Frost, First Sight
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sebastian and Rosalind collide at the frost-covered orchard at dawn, both drawn by the same gnarled trees named on the deed. Recognition lands like a physical blow; neither admits they've met before. Beat: the past made suddenly, dangerously present.

chapters.title: Ghostwriter's Rules
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He reviews his own rules: no real names, no entanglements, finish the book, leave. But Marguerite assigns him to shadow the harvest preparations — which means working beside Rosalind daily. Beat: discipline beginning to crack.

chapters.title: What the Vines Remember
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind walks Sebastian through the orchard, teaching him grafting, and lets slip fragments of a childhood promise made under the oldest tree — a promise Marguerite made to her late mother never to sell. She doesn't yet know why he flinches. Beat: intimacy through shared labor.

chapters.title: The Developer's Offer
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV (via interview). A luxury-resort developer, Callum Reeve, makes an offer that would rescue the vineyard's debts — if the orchard parcel is sold, which requires both names on the deed. Marguerite refuses; Rosalind, pragmatic, is tempted. Beat: money versus memory.

chapters.title: Lent Pieces
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian and Rosalind fall into an affair of carefully rationed honesty — he gives her everything but his history. A near-confession on the crush pad dies when Reeve appears, charming and knowing something about Sebastian's past. Beat: happiness built on a fault line.

chapters.title: Reeve's Leverage
chapters.summary: Reeve's POV. Reeve privately confronts Sebastian: he knows about the scandal that ended Sebastian's career and offers silence in exchange for steering the memoir toward a version favorable to the sale. Beat: corruption extending its hand.

chapters.title: The Chapter She Cut
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Transcribing Marguerite's tapes, Sebastian finds a deleted section: decades ago, Marguerite betrayed Rosalind's mother over this same orchard, breaking the promise the deed encodes. History is repeating itself through him. Beat: the theme of inherited betrayal crystallizes.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. On the eve of first harvest, Rosalind tells Sebastian she's leaning toward selling — the vineyard is drowning, and sentiment doesn't pay debts. She asks him, finally, to tell her one true thing about himself. He gives her a half-truth. Beat: love against duty, first fracture.

chapters.title: Exposed
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Reeve leaks Sebastian's identity and scandal to the local press, framing him as a fraud planted to manipulate the sale. Rosalind reads it before Sebastian can explain. Beat: the safe life collapses entirely.

chapters.title: What You Actually Wrote
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Humiliated, Rosalind finds Sebastian's draft manuscript hidden in the cottage — including the honest chapters about her, about Marguerite, about his own cowardice. She realizes the ghostwriter was the only one telling the truth. Beat: anger transmuting into understanding.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Confession
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Dying, Marguerite asks Sebastian to record the true final chapter: her betrayal of Rosalind's mother, the promise, and her hope that Rosalind will keep the land without inheriting the lie. Beat: memory reclaimed as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Signature Problem
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian discovers Reeve's purchase option rests on a forged signature — his own name was added to documents he never signed, tying him to the sale. Reporting it means breaching his confidentiality contract and ending his career for good. Beat: the choice sharpened to a point.

chapters.title: Risking the Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sebastian goes to Rosalind, confesses everything — the scandal, the half-truths, the forgery — and asks nothing except the chance to stand beside her. Rosalind must decide whether love can survive full disclosure. Beat: vulnerability as climax threshold.

chapters.title: The Night Before Harvest
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind chooses him. Together they plan to expose Reeve at the harvest festival, where he'll announce the resort — using Marguerite's recorded confession and the forged documents. Beat: allies at last, stakes maximal.

chapters.title: Festival of First Fruit
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Before the whole valley, Reeve unveils his plans; Sebastian publicly breaks his contract, presenting the forgery and playing Marguerite's tape. Reeve's financing collapses; the crowd turns. Beat: public climax, truth over safety.

chapters.title: Both Names
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. With Reeve gone, the deed question returns. Rosalind amends it to keep the orchard whole under the vineyard — and adds Sebastian's name beside hers, not as owner but as witness and partner. Marguerite dies at peace. Beat: grief braided with grace.

chapters.title: First Harvest Comes In
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The harvest succeeds against all odds; the first pressing happens with both of them working the press. Sebastian writes his first book under his own name — their story, with permission. Beat: reward earned through risk.

chapters.title: The Promise Kept
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, closing. One year later: the memoir publishes, the orchard bears its second crop, and Sebastian proposes beneath the oldest tree where the original promise was made. Safety, he understands now, was never small steps — it was a whole heart, freely given. Beat: resolution and thematic closure.
